title: Choosing his favorite pianist: his friend's genius
summary: He names his non-reading friend the best, able to copy any record and improve on it, with Pichon's ideas also admired.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Who was the, I guess you sort of picked your pianist saying Vernell, San Diego was the best and greatest you ever heard. Would you say that or who would be your favorite? Well. Of the New Orleans pianos.

I wouldn't have to say Vernell was my favorite piano player, although he couldn't read. But there was nothing that he heard that he couldn't play. I mean when Earl Hines was popular, he would, when he'd sit down at the piano he liked the kid, he would listen on it and he was a lot of fun. And he would listen at a record and he'd play like that record. Then he would play, then he'd say this is the way I would play it. And he'd play the way he would play it and it would get better and better all the time. So if he was a boy, well I guess if he knew music he wouldn't have had the ideas he had. But Pichon, his ideas were the greatest ideas I ever heard. Pichon wanted to teach him music if he would just show him some of the ideas that he had. See Pichon is a great writer of music. And boy he didn't want to learn how to read music or nothing like that. But I would have to say he's the best, although I mean he didn't play like the music would go, you know, but man he could play piano with his toes.

I'm not, I'm proud of, he'd take the back of his hand and play piano like that. I'd run with him all of his time. Him and I was just like brothers. Was he much older than you or any older? I was older than him.

Yeah, I was older than him. He was a young guy and a very good looking guy. He looked like something like an Indian. He had cold black hair. And he, man he had the fastest fingers. He played any kind of music.
He died when he was quite young. Yeah.
